title.narrative: Improvement of Water Access to mitigate La Nina induced drought impact in the high risk districts of Afmadow, Dhobley, Dinsor, Baidoa, Xudur and Quansax Dheere

description.narrative: The project will focus on ensuring that critical water sources are functional and resilient, providing essential support to areas hit hardest by the drought. This will include the emergency rehabilitation of 25 strategic water sources in the affected districts to restore reliable access to safe water for communities, the upgrade of 40 climate-resilient systems across drought-affected districts as well as the set-up of management systems. The rehabilitations will target non-functioning water systems and will involve repairs/ replacement of pumping system, reticulation systems, water tanks, and installation of equipment – pumps, solar panels and pipes. These upgrades will target sub-optimal water systems by improving the quality and sustainability of the water service as well as extending the water coverage to unserved households. The works will be very site specific and can include: solarization of pumping systems, extension of distribution networks and construction of water kiosks. All rehabilitated and upgraded infrastructure will be climate resilient by ensuring that they can adapt to changing climate conditions and maintain essential functions. This will be done through solarization, flood proofing (elevating borehole platforms), correct sizing of pumps and reservoirs (to maximize water storage), and water efficiency (through reduction of wastage, leaks and improved management). Where relevant, the project will work with the food security cluster to ensure rehabilitated assets are accessible for human and productive use. The WASH cluster will target the high priority drought prone districts identified by the UNICEF/FAO La Nina preparedness plan. This targeting has been carried out at the district level using robust, current and historical data from FSNAU and SWALIM, as well as WASH-related indicators monitored by UNICEF to identify the most drought-prone locations.
